```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(metamicrobiomeR)
```

While preparing version 2.0 we re-ran the examples of version 1.x. This page lists what we found, its effect and what
2.0 does about it. The script `data-raw/notes-earlier-results.R` in the source repository reproduces the numbers.

## The Coprococcus result in the sex-difference example

In the 1.x sex-difference example, the pooled Coprococcus result was an artefact. In the USA (NC) study, for infants up to
6 months, Coprococcus was non-zero in only 2 of 21 samples, one from each sex. The estimate therefore compares two values
(the logit difference between them is 0.4325, and the stored estimate is 0.4325), and its standard error (0.005) has no
inferential meaning. That study carried nearly all of the pooled weight. Without it the pooled p-value is 0.22, and no named
genus remains significant after false discovery rate correction.

You can see the weight problem from the data in the package:

```{r coprococcus}
data(tabsex4)
cop <- tabsex4[grepl("g__coprococcus$", tabsex4$id), c("pop", "Estimate.genderMale", "Std. Error.genderMale")]
cop
```

**In 2.0:** `taxa.compare()` warns about taxa with no more non-zero samples than mean-model coefficients, and
`meta.taxa()` warns when one study holds over 90% of the weight. In the modern layer, `fit_study()` does not fit such
features at all and lists them in `attr(, "low_support")`. The prevalence filter alone does not catch this, because 5%
of 21 samples is 1.05, so 2 non-zero samples pass.

## Other findings

| Finding | Effect | In 2.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Mixed-model p-values used `1.96 * pnorm(-abs(z))` in `taxa.compare()` and `pathway.compare()` | P-values were about 2% too small. In Table 3 of the 2019 paper, 0.0088 should be 0.0089. No conclusion changes. | Fixed |
| `meta.taxa()` counted rows, not studies with an estimate | For `bfNo_BF`, 82 of 185 "pooled" taxa came from one study and 4 from none. For `bfNon_exclusiveBF` and `age.sample`, 1 each. The sex term is unaffected. | Fixed |
| GAMLSS did not converge within the default 20 iterations in most fits | In the sex model on `taxtab6`, 109 of 124 taxa did not converge. Of 30 refitted at 300 iterations, all converged, the median p-value moved by 0.11 and 5 crossed 0.05. More iterations are not a full remedy, as they can give very small standard errors (below 0.05 in 24 CA/FL estimates at 100 iterations, against none at 20). | Warning, `n.cyc` argument, and a review of the modern engine |
| GAMLSS standard errors with a subject random effect can be too small | In null simulations of 40 subjects with 4 samples each and independent samples, GAMLSS-BEZI without `random()` kept the false-positive rate between 3% and 9%, which agrees with the cross-sectional simulations of 2019. With `random()`, the rate was 3% to 4% with no zeros and no subject effect, 34% for a between-subject variable with a subject effect and 40% of samples zero, and 55% to 83% with 85% of samples zero. On the real data in the 2019 example, standard errors at 20 iterations were close to those of a `glmmTMB` mixed model, so this does not by itself overturn those results, but sparse longitudinal estimates need caution. | Warning. `fit_study(engine = "bezi_glmmtmb")` fits the same model with a mixed-model likelihood. The default engine for longitudinal data is under review. |
| Adjusted p-values in the tables of the 2019 paper adjust within four phyla, while `taxa.compare()` adjusts across all taxa | For Actinobacteria in Example 1, the function gives 0.0571 and the table gives 0.0166. | Documented. `pool_effects()` makes the family of tests explicit. |
| Example 3 was fitted without the subject random effect | For Actinobacteria with exclusive breastfeeding up to 2 months, the estimate moves from -0.73 (p = 0.0003) to -0.60 (p = 0.0007) with it. For over 2 months, p moves from 0.92 to 0.41. The conclusions do not change. | Documented |
| Printing errors in the linear-model columns of Table 5 of the 2019 paper | In Example 3a, Bacteroidetes should be -0.06. In Example 3b, the Actinobacteria and Firmicutes rows are swapped. Nothing in that block is significant. | Documented |
| `taxa.compare()` gives covariates to the mean part of the zero-inflated beta model only | No group effect on the probability of absence is estimated. | Documented. `fit_study(engine = "zibb_glmmtmb", prevalence = ~ group)` estimates one. |
| `transform = "gmpr"` gave missing size factors for every sample | The option did not work. | Fixed |

## Reproducing the 1.x results

The legacy functions still give the 1.x numbers apart from the changes listed in `NEWS.md`. Reference tests compare them with
output from CRAN version 1.2 and with the stored pooled result of the 2019 sex-difference example.
